**task:** W2-55 (DAEO-arrl): the narrow review of S9, one relation check (D-6 part 2 item F2). Fresh, read-only reviewer on `w2/W2-55-f2` at `2fe928a4c`, compared against `b2b59caff`.

**status:** DONE. S9 **fails** on one in-scope finding, F1: after the change, no tool reports an unmarked `**Settles:**`. The test designer had already named this gap to the CTO.

**work_completed:**
- **Step 0 sandbox check: passes.** (a) Writing `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-W2-55` failed with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`. (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` worked (gave `1ae28402a109…`) and `git update-index --refresh` worked.
- **ps check:** no `ollama` or `llama-server` process is running. `ps -C ollama,llama-server` listed only this session's own shell.
- **What I read:** the S9 KPI line and the "D-6 part 2 item F2 placed here" note in `.tickets/DAEO-arrl.md`; `git diff b2b59caff..2fe928a4c` for `src/gov/decisions/tags.py`, `tests/unit/decisions/test_register_w2_55.py` and the S9 acceptance cases and README; `src/gov/util/register.py` (`gov.decisions.register` is the same module); `src/gov/store/loader.py` (`_OUT_LABELS`, `_entry_statements`, `register_statements`); `src/gov/links/check.py` (`_statements`, `unmarked`, `CHANGE_CLASSES`, `NOT_A_CHANGER`); LINK-INTEGRITY §1 item 5, §2.2 and the W2-55 note; DEC-866.
- **What I ran:** the loader's `register_statements` on each relation label, to see how `gov links` classes it.

**files_changed:** none.

**evidence:**
- `register_statements` with `gov links`' `CHANGE_CLASSES`, one call per label:
  - `Supersedes` → supersede, counted.
  - `Changes` → amend, counted.
  - `Settles` → **settle, not counted**.
  - `Corrects` → amend, counted.
  - `Reverses` → supersede, counted.
  - `Withdraws` → supersede, counted.
- A partial `Supersedes` (`the last point of DEC-115`, `DEC-115 (item 2)`) → supersede, part, counted. `DEC-115 and DEC-114` → two whole supersessions, counted.
- The real register has 4 `**Settles:**` labels, at lines 789, 3829, 3873 and 9100. Every entry they settle carries `**Changed by:** settled by DEC-n`, at lines 62, 2868, 3690 and 9047.
- `du --inodes` of my TMPDIR: 10. I made one empty folder, `$TMPDIR/home-empty`, and nothing else.

**tests:**
- I could not re-run pytest: the sandbox's `python3` has no pytest module ("No module named pytest"), and installing it is not allowed.
- The runs in the brief stand as reported, not re-checked: `gov accept W2-55` 55 passed, 3 failed (the 3 are backfill cases, red on the base too); `tests/acceptance/W2-129` 150/0; `tests/unit/decisions` 37/0.
- Because nothing ran, the real-model exclusion left out nothing.

**discoveries:**
- `Settles` is a change in W2-55's own register module: it is in `register.py`'s `CHANGING`, and the module's docstring says "`**Settles:**` ... change".
- It is also a change in practice: DEC-825 marked every settlement with `Changed by: settled by`, and DEC-866 (1) says the old entry is marked "whenever a decision supersedes, cancels or changes another".
- `gov links` classes it as "settle", and LINK-INTEGRITY §2.2 row 118 says "settles ... Required by: nothing ... none (not a change)".
- So the two sources disagree. The removed loop was the only check that caught an unmarked settlement.

**risks:** F1. An entry an honest agent writes with `**Settles:** DEC-x`, and no mark on DEC-x, is now caught by nothing. The in-force digest still names the settler, because `register.py`'s `changed` still reads `Settles` from the settler's side.

**lessons:** a removal that hands a check over to "the same relation" in another tool needs each form mapped one to one before the KPI states the two are equal. The test designer did that mapping and named the gap; the KPI line went ahead without it.

**proposed_decisions:** F1 for the CTO, three costed options (DEC-105):
- **(a) Apply now:** add `"settle"` to `CHANGE_CLASSES` in `src/gov/links/check.py`. It is one word, but in W2-129's file, so outside W2-55's paths. It would need a W2-129 case and a `gov links` run on the real register to count any new findings, for example from free-text "settled by".
- **(b) Defer:** record a Wave 3 row and add a line to the S9 KPI saying `Settles` is left out, by LINK-INTEGRITY §2.2.
- **(c) Re-baseline:** amend LINK-INTEGRITY §2.2 and DEC-866's reading so that a settlement needs no mark, and change `register.py`'s `CHANGING` to match.

My recommendation is (a), with medium confidence: it matches DEC-866 and the register's own practice, and it costs very little.

**unresolved:** whether a settlement is a change is a decision for the CTO or the owner, and it decides whether F1 blocks. I could not re-run the tests myself.

**recommended_next_action:** the CTO chooses (a), (b) or (c) for F1. With (a) or (c), S9 is re-checked; with (b), F1 becomes a row and S9 can be re-judged as passing.

---

### Check 1: nothing else changes in `check_tags`
**Yes, nothing else changes.**
- The diff removes only the `for relation, olds in ...` loop and rewrites the docstring's description of it.
- `_tag_findings` is untouched, so `TAG_MISSING`, `TAG_DOMAIN_UNKNOWN`, `TAG_SCOPE_UNKNOWN`, `TAG_LANDS_IN_UNKNOWN` and `TAG_LANDS_IN_MISPLACED` keep their messages.
- `STATUS_SUCCESSOR_UNNAMED`'s condition and message are the same.
- The order is the same: `sorted(found, key=(code, ids, paths))`.
- `held` is still used, by the successor check.
- The unit case now expects `[("STATUS_SUCCESSOR_UNNAMED", ("DEC-102",))]` and checks that the removed code is absent.
- The fields only the removed loop read (`named`, plus `supersedes`/`changes` for this purpose) stay in `register.py`. `named` now has no reader; that is harmless.

### Check 2: is the relation still reported by one tool?
**Not for every form.**

| Form the removed loop caught | `gov links` UNMARKED_CHANGE |
|---|---|
| `**Supersedes:**` with ids alone | yes (supersede, whole) |
| `**Supersedes:**` naming a part | yes (supersede, part) |
| `**Changes:**` | yes (amend) |
| `**Settles:**` | **no: class "settle" is not in `CHANGE_CLASSES` (F1)** |
| `**Corrects:**` | yes (amend) |
| `**Reverses:**` | yes (supersede) |
| `**Withdraws:**` | yes (supersede) |

Other differences, none of them a lost form:
- **Where it looks:** `gov links` reads labels anywhere in the entry, and free text and the change log too. The removed loop read the status line only.
- **Which sources count:** `gov links` ignores a source whose status is PROPOSED, REJECTED or WITHDRAWN (`NOT_A_CHANGER`); the removed loop did not. A proposal changes nothing yet, so this is the correct reading (row F3).
- **When the old entry counts as marked:** `gov links` treats it as marked if the new id appears anywhere on its status line. The removed loop needed the id in `**Changed by:**` or in the status word (row F2).
- **Id width:** the loader's `_DEC` needs 3 or more digits. Every real id has 3 or more (`DEC-004`), so this changes nothing.

### Check 3: out-of-date text (rows only)
- F4: `.tickets/DAEO-q7lk.md:79` still names `gov.decisions.tags` (`STATUS_RELATION_UNMARKED`).
- F5: `LINK-INTEGRITY.md:67` ("66 today ... The CTO runs it after each decision record") and `:423` (the note on its relation check).
- F6: `LINK-INTEGRITY-tickets/W2-129-gov-links.md:73`.
- F7: `tests/acceptance/W2-55/w2_55_support.py:48` keeps the code in `TAG_CODES`. It is harmless as a list of known codes, but out of date.

### Findings
**F1 — no tool reports an unmarked `**Settles:**` after S9** (`src/gov/decisions/tags.py`, the removed loop; `src/gov/links/check.py:75`). Scope: in, because S9's KPI says an entry that "supersedes or changes" another is "reported by gov links alone", and `Settles` is a change in `register.py` and by DEC-866 (1).
Ordinary work: yes, because the register already holds 4 `**Settles:**` status labels, and an honest agent writing a fifth can forget to mark the old entry.
Consequence: fails open. The removed check caught that unmarked entry; nothing catches it now.

**F2 — `gov links` treats an old entry as marked if the new id appears anywhere on its status line**, for example in `**Basis:**`. Scope: out (W2-129's own rule).
Ordinary work: no, because an old entry's status line names a later entry, in practice, only to mark it.
Consequence: other.

**F3 — `gov links` does not count a PROPOSED, REJECTED or WITHDRAWN entry as a changer; the removed loop did.** Scope: out (W2-129's own rule).
Ordinary work: yes, because a proposal can carry a `**Supersedes:**` label.
Consequence: other. A proposal changes nothing until it is accepted, so no mark is due yet.

**F4 to F7 — out-of-date text naming `STATUS_RELATION_UNMARKED`** (the places in check 3). Scope: out.
Ordinary work: yes, because readers of the ticket and of LINK-INTEGRITY meet the text.
Consequence: other. It is wording only; nothing runs on it.
